name: Co-Creating the Programme — Trinity Quad Executive Learning
description: A four-round, advanced executive-education simulation set inside Trinity Quad Executive Learning, the custom-programmes unit of a leading UK business school in Cambridge (£14.2M revenue, 32% contribution margin, NPS 71, 60% repeat revenue). On 14 September 2026, Helvern Industrial Group — a £3.8bn FTSE-250 engineering firm — signs a £680,000 custom contract to build strategic leadership capability across 90 senior managers (3 cohorts of 30) ahead of a restructuring, and wants cohort 1 live in 10 weeks. As Custom Programmes Director you must (1) diagnose the real challenge from a one-paragraph brief and three conflicting sponsor views — the CEO means post-restructuring strategic alignment, the CHRO means high-potential retention, line directors mean project-delivery discipline — before designing anything; (2) co-configure a tailored learning journey within the £680k envelope, choosing pedagogy mix, faculty from a scarcity-and-cost grid (only 2 of 5 preferred senior faculty are free; core faculty £2,200/day vs star practitioners £4,500/day), and a delivery format whose cost swings £90,000; (3) defend the price premium against procurement's £5,500/participant benchmark (27% below the £7,556 as-designed cost) and commit to or renegotiate the £68,000 (10%) impact-linked success fee; and (4) deliver cohort 1 through a faculty drop-out and patchy attendance, then design the impact-measurement approach (reaction, behaviour or results, on the Kirkpatrick ladder) that releases the success fee and decide whether to run cohorts 2–3 (worth £453,000). The math rewards diagnosing before designing, 70-20-10 journeys that embed action-learning and coaching, defending value rather than discounting, Behaviour/Results-level measurement, and treating resourcing as a quality decision — and punishes the five classic errors. Final KPIs track Diagnosis Fit, Impact Credibility, Client Trust, and contribution Margin against the £680k cap.
view:
14 September 2026 · Trinity Quad Executive Learning, Cambridge · Helvern Industrial Group — £680k, 90 managers, cohort 1 live in 10 weeks

Co-Creating the Programme

A £3.8bn FTSE-250 engineer has signed a £680,000 custom contract to "build strategic leadership capability" across 90 senior managers ahead of a restructuring. The brief is one paragraph of generic ambition; the real challenge is buried, the budget is fixed, the faculty are oversubscribed, and a £68,000 success fee is tied to measurable impact. Diagnose it, co-design it, defend it, deliver it.

Your Decisions This Round

Insistence on diagnosing the need before committing the solution: 60
Core faculty days — £2,200/day · available, solid relevance
Star practitioner days — £4,500/day · high relevance, scarce (2 of 5 free)
Faculty spend: £186k
Design + measurement build is fixed at £120k. Watch cost per participant against the £7,556 design point and the £5,500 benchmark.
Design value conceded to procurement: 15
Facilitator (Helvern's sponsor & procurement lead)
The brief asks for "a leadership course". But the CEO means post-restructuring alignment, the CHRO means high-potential retention, and the line directors mean delivery discipline — design for the wrong one and £680k buys a well-reviewed irrelevance. Diagnose the real need before you design, build a journey that produces behaviour change rather than teaching days, defend the value of that journey instead of discounting it to the £5,500 benchmark, and prove the impact that releases the £68k success fee.
